newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle set new contract highs, then slip.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle set new contract highs, then slip.

text.p: CME live cattle futures continued to climb and quickly posted new contract highs for the third consecutive day in the February and April contracts before turning lower in early dealings.
Feeder cattle started mixed and then fell.
Carryover demand on strong cash markets lifted live cattle but profit taking developed and turned prices lower, traders said. Feeder cattle also retreated from a mixed start.

At 0908 CST, live cattle stood 0.050 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower with only February holding a gain and April off 0.075 at 68.625 cents. February had posted a new high of 67.900 cents and April, 68.975 cents.
Feeder cattle were off 0.050 to 0.300 cent per lb with March off 0.050 at 68.150 cents.
